title: Composition
subtitle: Functions inside functions: building them and taking them apart.

questions.text: $f(g(x))$ and $g(f(x))$ are always the same function.
questions.explain: With $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = x + 3$: $(x + 3)^2$ and $x^2 + 3$ are different.

questions.text: $f(g(x))$ means $f(x) · g(x)$.
questions.explain: It is not multiplication. $g(x)$ is the **input** of $f$.

questions.text: The inside function of $(3x - 1)^5$ is
questions.explain: You compute $3x - 1$ first, then raise it to the 5th power.

questions.text: The inside function of $e^(x^2)$ is
questions.explain: You square $x$ first, then use it as the exponent.

questions.text: $sin^2(x)$ means $(sin(x))^2$. Its inside function is
questions.explain: Take the sine first, then square the result. The outside is $u^2$.

questions.text: The **outside** function of $ln(4x + 1)$ is
questions.explain: The last thing you do is take the logarithm.

slides.text:
$f(g(x))$ means: do $g$ first, then put its answer into $f$.$$g(2) = 5,    f(5) = 11$$
What is $f(g(2))$?
slides.label: $f(g(2))$ =
slides.explain: $f(g(2)) = f(5) = 11$. Always work from the inside out.

slides.text:
$$f(x) = x^2,    g(x) = x + 3$$
As a formula, $f(g(x))$ puts **all** of $g(x)$ into the blank of $f$. Type what goes in the blank.
slides.label: In the blank:
slides.hint: The blank gets the whole formula for $g(x)$.

slides.text: Order matters. With the same $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = x + 3$, what is $g(f(x))$?
slides.hint: Now $f(x)$ goes into the blank of $g$.
slides.explain: $g(f(x)) = x^2 + 3$, which is not $(x + 3)^2$. Swapping the order changes the function.

slides.text:
Now run it backwards.$$h(x) = sqrt(x^2 + 1)$$
If you plugged in a number, what would you compute **first**? That part is the inside function.
slides.hint: You cannot take the square root until you know what is under it.
slides.explain: Inside: $x^2 + 1$. It gets computed first, then handed to the square root.

slides.text:
$$h(x) = sqrt(x^2 + 1)$$
The outside function is what you do **last**. Call the inside $u = x^2 + 1$. Write the outside as a function of $u$.
slides.label: $f(u)$ =
slides.hint: Once you have $u$, all that is left is to take its square root.
slides.explain: $h(x) = f(g(x))$ with inside $g(x) = x^2 + 1$ and outside $f(u) = sqrt(u)$.
